hints.title: Multiplication Precedence Immediate Evaluation Obstacle
hints.text: Evaluating left-to-right naively ignores standard operator precedence between addition and multiplication. How can storing pending terms allow you to resolve multiplications and divisions before sum aggregation?

hints.title: Immediate Precedence Resolution Invariant
hints.text: Evaluate * and / immediately with the last processed number, while pushing + and - operands to sum at the end.

hints.title: Operator Buffer Processing Procedure
hints.text: Track currentNumber and lastSign (default '+'). When an operator or string end is reached: if lastSign is '+', push num. If '-', push -num. If '*', pop and multiply with num. If '/', pop and truncate toward zero with num. Reset num and update lastSign. Sum all numbers at the end.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 3 * 10^5)
complexity.notes: Single pass resolving high-precedence operators immediately.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full recursive parsing or nested regex evaluation times out on strings with 300,000 characters.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Pending operand buffering enables strictly linear time evaluation without building an expression tree.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct integer division truncation toward zero (e.g. -3 // 2 in Python truncates to -2, requiring int(-3 / 2)).
